studies.Reference: Food groups and renal cell carcinoma: a case-control study from Italy.
studies.Title: Food groups and renal cell carcinoma: a case-control study from Italy.
studies.Authors: Bravi F, Bosetti C, Scotti L, Talamini R, Montella M, Ramazzotti V, Negri E, Franceschi S, La Vecchia C
studies.Timing: Dietary habits 2 years before diagnosis or hospital admission
studies.Population: Patients with incident, histologically confirmed renal cell carcinoma and hospital controls with acute non-neoplastic conditions

sample_size.excerpt: We evaluated the relation between a wide range of foods and the risk of RCC in an Italian case-control study including 767 patients (494 men and 273 women) younger than 79 years with incident, histologically confirmed RCC, and 1,534 controls (988 men and 546 women) admitted to the same hospitals as cases for a wide spectrum of acute, non-neoplastic conditions, not related to long term diet modifications.
sample_size.location: abstract, methods; total_n derived from reported group counts 767 + 1534 = 2301

cases.excerpt: We evaluated the relation between a wide range of foods and the risk of RCC in an Italian case-control study including 767 patients (494 men and 273 women) younger than 79 years with incident, histologically confirmed RCC, and 1,534 controls (988 men and 546 women) admitted to the same hospitals as cases for a wide spectrum of acute, non-neoplastic conditions, not related to long term diet modifications.

effect_size.excerpt: No relation was found for coffee and tea, soups, eggs, red meat, fish, cheese, pulses, potatoes, fruits, desserts and sugars.

comparison.excerpt: OR = 1.94 for the highest versus the lowest intake quintile

timing.excerpt: to assess patients' dietary habits 2 years before diagnosis or hospital admission

exposure_measurement.excerpt: A validated and reproducible food frequency questionnaire, including 78 foods and beverages

studies.Reference: Intake of fiber and fiber-rich plant foods is associated with a lower risk of renal cell carcinoma in a large US cohort.
studies.Title: Intake of fiber and fiber-rich plant foods is associated with a lower risk of renal cell carcinoma in a large US cohort.
studies.Authors: Daniel CR, Park Y, Chow WH, Graubard BI, Hollenbeck AR, Sinha R
studies.Journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
studies.Population: NIH-AARP Diet and Health Study participants
studies.Smoking Status: Overall cohort; association was consistent among never smokers
studies.comparison_type: Highest versus lowest quintile of legume intake

sample_size.excerpt: Participants of the NIH-AARP Diet and Health Study (n = 491,841) completed a self-administered questionnaire of demographics, diet, lifestyle, and medical history. Over 9 (mean) years of follow-up we identified 1816 incident cases of RCC.

cases.excerpt: Over 9 (mean) years of follow-up we identified 1816 incident cases of RCC.

comparison.excerpt: Intakes of legumes, whole grains, and cruciferous vegetables were also associated with a 16-18% reduced risk of RCC.

design.excerpt: In a large prospective cohort of US men and women, we comprehensively investigated dietary intake and food sources of fiber in relation to RCC risk.

continent.excerpt: In a large prospective cohort of US men and women

exposure_measurement.excerpt: completed a self-administered questionnaire of demographics, diet, lifestyle, and medical history

smoking_status.excerpt: The inverse association between fiber intake and RCC was consistent among participants who never smoked
